meta.title: Flights taking off in a day from Delhi Airport

prompt: Estimate the number of flights taking off in a day from Delhi Airport.

clarifications.answer: Count only commercial passenger flights; ignore seasonal surges, cargo and military.
Assume about 80 boarding gates, with one take-off (including boarding) per gate per hour.
Split the day into 8 peak hours (80% gates used), 12 non-peak hours (50% gates used) and 4 non-operational hours (0).
Use a supply-side approach: gate capacity by time band.

common_traps: Assuming full gate utilisation all day instead of splitting into peak / non-peak / non-operational.
Forgetting the ~1 hour take-off gap per gate, so gate count is not converted into flights per hour.
Counting arrivals as well as departures when the question asks only for take-offs.

anchors.1: Guesses a number with no gate-capacity reasoning.
anchors.3: Uses gates x hours but at one flat utilisation across the whole day.
anchors.5: Applies gate capacity per time band with distinct utilisation for peak and non-peak hours.

anchors.1: No split of the day into time bands.
anchors.3: Splits hours but with utilisation rates not clearly reasoned.
anchors.5: Splits the day into peak / non-peak / non-operational with sensible utilisation for each.

anchors.1: Errors in the gates-times-hours-times-utilisation product; lands far off.
anchors.3: Reaches a number with a slip, landing just outside 700-1300.
anchors.5: Carries the per-band math cleanly, landing near 1000 flights.

anchors.3: Mentions a check but does not complete it.
anchors.5: Back-checks via passengers: ~1000 flights x ~120 seats implies ~1 lakh daily flyers, which is reasonable for Delhi.
